Plan to add three new regression tests in PricingCalculatorTest.java covering the 10,000-cent bulk-discount threshold at 9,999 (no discount), 10,000 (discount applies), and 10,001 (discount applies) cents for a REGULAR-tier order, without touching any production code, then run the focused tests via Maven.

Implementation steps:
1. Confirm the threshold logic in DiscountPolicy.discountRate: subtotalCents >= 10_000 triggers a 10% discount for REGULAR customers (VIP always gets 20%, so use REGULAR tier orders for these tests).
2. In /src/test/java/com/sweforge/pricing/PricingCalculatorTest.java, add a @Test method for subtotal 9,999 cents (single Item(9_999)) asserting the total equals 9,999 (no discount, since 9,999 < 10,000).
3. Add a @Test method for subtotal exactly 10,000 cents (single Item(10_000)) asserting the total equals 9,000 (10% discount applied at the boundary, since 10,000 >= 10,000).
4. Add a @Test method for subtotal 10,001 cents (single Item(10_001)) asserting the total equals 9,001 rounded per Math.round(10_001 * 0.90) = 9,001 (10% discount applied above the boundary).
5. Follow existing test conventions: use the shared 'calculator' field, List.of(...) for items, default REGULAR tier via the single-arg Order constructor, and assertEquals(expected, actual) formatting consistent with existing tests.
6. Do not modify DiscountPolicy.java, PricingCalculator.java, or any other production source file — this is a test-only change.
7. Run the focused test class (e.g., mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test) under Java 21 to verify the three new boundary tests and existing tests pass, then run the full 'mvn test' suite as a final validation per the pricing-build-validation skill.

Validation:
- mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test passes with all 6 tests (3 existing + 3 new) green
- mvn test (full suite) passes with no failures
- Diff shows changes only in PricingCalculatorTest.java; no production files under src/main modified
- New tests explicitly cover subtotal values 9_999, 10_000, and 10_001 cents
